Question:
Trapezoid \(ABCD\) has \(\overline{AB}\parallel\overline{CD},\) \(BC=CD=43,\) and \(\overline{AD}\perp\overline{BD}.\) Let \(O\) be the intersection of the diagonals \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{BD},\) and let \(P\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{BD}.\)

Given that \(OP=11,\) the length of \(AD\) can be written in the form \(m\sqrt{n},\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are positive integers and \(n\) is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(m+n?\)
Solution:
Use the equal sides \(BC=CD\) to find a useful perpendicular. In isosceles triangle \(BCD\), the median \(CP\) to base \(BD\) is perpendicular to \(BD\). Since \(AD\perp BD\) as well, \(CP\parallel AD\).

[Figure 1](figures/2021_AMC_10A_Q17_official_solution_fig1.png)

Triangles \(BDA\) and \(DPC\) are similar: \(BD\) and \(DP\) lie on the same line, \(DA\parallel PC\), and \(BA\parallel DC\). As \(P\) is the midpoint of \(BD\), their scale factor is \(BD/DP=2\). Therefore \(AB=2CD=86\).

Now triangles \(AOB\) and \(COD\) are similar, using the parallel bases and vertical angles at \(O\). Thus
\[
\frac{BO}{DO}=\frac{AB}{CD}=2,
\]
so \(DO=BD/3\). Since \(DP=BD/2\), the distance from \(O\) to \(P\) is \(BD/2-BD/3=BD/6\). Given \(OP=11\), this gives \(BD=66\).

Triangle \(ADB\) is right-angled at \(D\), so
\[
AD=\sqrt{86^2-66^2}=\sqrt{3040}=4\sqrt{190}.
\]
The integer \(190=2\cdot5\cdot19\) is square-free. Hence \(m+n=4+190=\boxed{194}\), choice D. Equal sides identify a median, while parallel lines let its half-length relation control the rest of the figure.
